topics.topic: Complete set of mapping inputs bound by import confirmation
questions: Does the confirmation bind only upload number, digest and project picks, or also every display name, alias, Customer name, kind and tax-id choice that A16 says the shown mapping fixes?

Does “the picks” include the complete mapping inputs required by A16—project selections, replacement display names, aliases, and every Customer name, kind, and tax-id choice—or only the selected project identities?

Does the binding also cover every displayed and submitted display name, alias, Customer name, Customer kind and tax-id choice required by A16, and must a submission differing in any of them be refused rather than applied?

The upload's number in the session: 1 for the session's first accepted
upload, then one more than the session's last, so two uploads of the same
bytes are two uploads (A16 rule 2).
The kept file's bytes, digest and upload number, or that none is kept.
judgement.why: The later owner_sessions API defines a per-session increasing upload number, changes it for identical replacement uploads, and stores and returns it with the kept file.

topics.topic: Exact OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS rows, discriminators, matching key, and uniqueness behavior

What is the complete, unique set of rows, which discriminator is required for each owner action, and what happens when no row or more than one row matches?

When OwnerAuditAction carries a CustomerTransition or ProjectErasure discriminator, is the row selected by OwnerAction alone or by the composite key of OwnerAction plus the applicable transition or erasure kind, and what uniqueness rule does the table enforce?

quotes:
`OwnerAuditAction` (an owner action,
a customer mark's transition or a project erasure's kind where the action
has one, and the audit action it writes) with `OwnerAction`,
`CustomerTransition`, `ProjectErasure` and `AuditAction` for
`OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS`.

topics.topic: Exact staged-close time and byte limit values and numeric constraints
questions: What exact release values must `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS` and `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_MAX_BYTES` hold?
What exact values and numeric types do `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS` and `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_MAX_BYTES` have, and are zero or fractional seconds admissible?
What exact positive values must LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS and LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_MAX_BYTES have?

quotes:
That close is staged (RFC 9112 section 9.6; owner, 2026-11-24): after the
answer is written the listener shuts the socket's writing side, then reads
and drops what the client still sends until the client closes, the imported
`LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS` (2) have passed since the shutdown, or the
imported `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB) have been dropped,
whichever comes first, and only then closes the socket.
judgement.why: The later contract fixes the drain duration at 2 seconds and the byte cap at 64 MiB.

topics.topic: Staged-close drain termination, deadline precedence, and byte accounting
questions: When does the drain timer start, does reaching either bound end the drain, how are EOF and read errors handled, does `LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` also apply, and do already-buffered unread body bytes count toward the byte bound?

Does draining stop at the first of EOF, the current request body's framed end, the time limit, and the byte limit; do counted bytes include chunk framing and bytes of a pipelined next request; and is the connection always closed once the current body ends?

During staged close, does `LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` still apply to each read, or is it replaced by the single `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS` deadline; when does that deadline start and which clock measures it?
Which bytes count against LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_MAX_BYTES: transport bytes, TLS-decoded HTTP wire bytes including chunk framing, or decoded body payload bytes?

During a staged close, does LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS still terminate an individual stalled read, or is LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS the sole time bound until the body ends or the byte bound is reached?

quotes:
what the
client still sends read and dropped up to the data provider's
`LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS` and `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_MAX_BYTES`, then
closed
judgement.why: Timer precedence, read-timeout interaction, framed-end handling and the layer at which bytes are counted are operational connection-contract details owned by State 6, not module-ownership questions for State 3.

topics.topic: Which accepted owner actions require audit entries, including no-op actions
questions: Does “each accepted owner action” mean every accepted invocation, or only an accepted action that changes state, plus the special audit-erasure case required by A14 and A15?

Does `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` cover only accepted state-changing owner actions that M09 and A14 say write an entry, or does every accepted owner action, including reads and unchanged transitions, write one?

Is OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS a sparse table containing only M09 actions that actually write an entry after a state change, or a total table covering reads and accepted no-op owner actions as well; if total, how is “no audit entry” represented?

quotes:
A14 rules 1 and 5:
appending the audit entry in the action's transaction when the action changed
state, its action the row of the data provider's `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` for
an owner action (owner, 2026-11-24).

A05 rule 2's no entry and no
confirmation id for a repeat.

An erasure that removes no entry still writes its own entry naming the
date, with its confirmation id: R0-66 makes the erasure leave an entry of
its own, whatever it removed. It is the one accepted action that writes an
entry without changing other state (A14 rule 3).
judgement.why: The texts limit ordinary audit writes to accepted state changes, expressly exclude unchanged repeats, and identify erasure of old audit entries as the sole no-change exception.

Declare `operations` → `data_provider` → `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` in `module_internal`, or rewrite the passage so `operations` does not directly name or use that export.

quotes:
The entry through
`audit_log.append_audit_entry` only when the action changed state and M09
lists it — the row of the imported `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` constant for the
action, with a customer mark's transition or a project erasure's kind, and
for an answer to an access request only when it granted a project (M09;
owner, 2026-11-24) — and for an erasure of old entries after

judgement.why: The later dependency table explicitly declares operations' direct import of OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS, while the surface text assigns operations the row selection and leaves data_provider as the constant's owner.

topics.topic: Whether AuditEntry receives the matched row or its AuditAction field, and who projects it
questions: Is `AuditEntry.change` the matched row itself or the row's `AuditAction` field, and which module performs that projection?
Must AuditEntry.action receive the row's AuditAction field, or the entire OwnerAuditAction row?

quotes:
The transaction; the action, from M09's closed vocabulary; its subject by
identity — the project, the customer, the session and the project, the
import's file digest, or none for an erasure of old entries; the acting
principal; the action's instant; the confirmation id when one was minted;

judgement.why: The later append API takes M09's action value rather than an OwnerAuditAction row, and names operations as the caller that performs the projection before appending.

quotes:
That close is staged (RFC 9112 section 9.6; owner, 2026-11-24): after the
answer is written the listener shuts the socket's writing side, then reads
and drops what the client still sends until the client closes, the imported
`LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS` (2) have passed since the shutdown, or the

a request answered before its body was read to its end

topics.topic: Which early-response and framing-error cases require staged close
questions: Which early answers use staged close, especially header-level refusals with malformed `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding`, stream failures from malformed chunks, authentication refusals, and requests whose framing has no knowable body end?

quotes:
a request whose `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding`
header is malformed is refused by the listener from its headers alone, its
connection closed, and reaches no surface; the body itself is never read
ahead by the listener, so a body that ends before its framing says, or
whose chunks are malformed, is a failure of the stream its reader sees
while reading it; a request answered before its body was read to its end
closes its connection by a staged close — its writing side shut, what the
client still sends read and dropped up to the data provider's
`LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_SECONDS` and `LISTENER_CLOSE_DRAIN_MAX_BYTES`, then
closed — so the answer reaches a client still sending its body (RFC 9112
section 9.6; owner, 2026-11-24);
judgement.why: The text separately assigns malformed framing to listener refusal and closure, exposes premature ends and malformed chunks as stream failures, and applies staged close generally whenever an answer is produced before the body reaches its end.
